stories.title: Tishman Speyer Sells SoHo Offices to Shorenstein
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer has sold 148 Lafayette St., a fully leased, 12-story, Class A boutique office building in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, for $132.5 million to Shorenstein Properties. Marking its first U.S. office acquisition since 2021, Tishman Speyer acquired 148 Lafayette for $105.5 million just 17 months earlier. “We acquired 148 Lafayette with a clear plan and executed it ahead of schedule, generating an attractive return for our investors,” said Tishman Speyer Senior Managing Director Chris Shehadeh. “This successful outcome reaffirms our conviction in the continued demand for premier office assets in prime Manhattan neighborhoods to both companies seeking exceptional work environments and institutional investors targeting high-quality real estate.” Tishman Speyer was represented in the transaction by Adam Spies and Avery Silverstein of Newmark. Built in 1913 and renovated in 2017, 148 Lafayette is within short walking distance of seven subway lines, SoHo’s wide range of luxury residences and shopping, dining, educational and cultural venues. The post Tishman Speyer Sells SoHo Offices to Shorenstein appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tishman Speyer sold 148 Lafayette St., SoHo, to Shorenstein for $132.5M.
Tishman purchased same asset 17 months prior for $105.5M; $27M gain realized.
First U.S. office acquisition by Tishman since 2021; signals renewed institutional confidence in prime Manhattan office.
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer exited a fully leased, Class A SoHo office building (148 Lafayette St., 155,000 SF) to Shorenstein Properties for $132.5M ($866/SF), just 17 months after acquiring it for $105.5M in May 2025—a $27M profit. The sale marks Tishman's first U.S. office deal since 2021 and comes amid active competitive bidding from institutional investors. The building, built in 1913 and renovated in 2017, sits in prime SoHo with proximity to seven subway lines.
stories.impact: Institutional investors (Shorenstein, PE funds) are actively bidding for fully leased, trophy office assets in Manhattan's prime neighborhoods, suggesting selective recovery in Class A office valuations in high-barrier-to-entry locations. This flip signals that well-capitalized developers can time office acquisitions for quick value realization when market confidence returns; however, broader office headwinds mean this play is limited to A-tier, transit-rich assets in SoHo/downtown Manhattan with strong tenant rosters—not a signal of wide-spread office recovery.

stories.title: Truist Closes Construction Loan for Long Beach Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Truist recently closed a $152-million construction loan for Marina Shores, a 390-unit multifamily community at 6615 E. Pacific Coast Hwy. in Long Beach. The project is being developed by Carmel Partners. The six-story project will transform an aging office complex and surface lot into a mixed-income community with approximately 5,400 square feet of ground-floor retail space. It is part of a major revitalization effort along the Pacific Coast Highway, which is seeing significant residential developments. “Marina Shores brings together experienced sponsorship, strong market fundamentals, and an opportunity to deliver much-needed housing in Long Beach,” said Rebecca M. Cox, SVP and Market Manager, Truist National Real Estate. Truist served as administrative agent and sole bookrunner on the $152-million development loan. The transaction was led by Jason Paxton, Mid-Atlantic market leader, with Walt Reece, a director on the Real Estate Syndicated Finance team at Truist Securities, leading syndication efforts. Rendering courtesy of SCB. The post Truist Closes Construction Loan for Long Beach Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Truist closed $152M construction loan for Marina Shores, 390-unit multifamily in Long Beach.
Carmel Partners developing mixed-income community; 5,400 SF retail; adaptive reuse of office complex.
Part of major Pacific Coast Highway revitalization effort; strong market fundamentals cited by lender.
stories.summary: Truist closed a $152M construction loan for Marina Shores, a 390-unit multifamily community in Long Beach (6615 E. Pacific Coast Hwy.), being developed by Carmel Partners. The six-story project converts an aging office complex into mixed-income housing with ground-floor retail. Truist acted as administrative agent and sole bookrunner, syndicated the loan, and emphasized strong market fundamentals and robust sponsorship.
stories.impact: Long Beach Pacific Coast Highway corridor is seeing institutional construction financing and mixed-income multifamily development, signaling lender confidence in coastal Southern California demand. This conversion of underutilized office to rental housing reflects broader adaptive-reuse opportunity in Southern California coastal markets where office conversion economics work and mixed-income entitlements are feasible—an early signal of where obsolete office stock can be productively recycled into high-demand rental supply in supply-constrained West Coast metros.

stories.title: Merchants Bank Retains CBRE to Market Fee Interest in Midtown Residential Property
stories.excerpt: CBRE has been retained by Merchants Bank to market for sale the fee interest in 19 W. 55th St., a vacant, nine-story residential property with continuous retail frontage in Midtown Manhattan. CBRE’s Daniel Kaplan was appointed by the bank to spearhead the sale. “Opportunities to acquire the fee interest of an asset in this premier Midtown location are limited,” said Kaplan. “19 W. 55th St. offers investors the ability to own a strategically located property in one of the most coveted corridors in New York City.” Once known as The Branson, 19 W. 55th St. was built in 1920 and comprises 39,000 square feet. According to published reports, Merchants Bank foreclosed on the property, which its previous owner had sought to convert into luxury condominiums, this past July following delays due to the developer filing for Chapter 11 protection on two separate occasions. The post Merchants Bank Retains CBRE to Market Fee Interest in Midtown Residential Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Merchants Bank foreclosed on 19 W. 55th St., Midtown Manhattan vacant 9-story residential property.
Previous developer filed Chapter 11 twice; condo conversion stalled; lender marketing fee interest for sale.
39,000 SF asset; 1920 vintage; retail frontage in coveted Midtown corridor.
stories.summary: Merchants Bank, which foreclosed on 19 W. 55th St. in July 2026 after the developer filed for Chapter 11 protection twice, has retained CBRE to market the fee interest for sale. The 39,000 SF property, built in 1920 and known as The Branson, is a nine-story residential asset with continuous retail frontage in Midtown Manhattan. The previous owner had attempted a luxury condo conversion before failing.
stories.impact: Distressed residential conversion/development in Midtown Manhattan is surfacing as condo market deterioration and financing tightness force developer bankruptcies; this creates opportunistic acquisition windows for multifamily operators or experienced conversion teams with strong capital access. The fee interest sale structure signals lender willingness to accept lower recovery, creating potential entry points for sophisticated sponsors to acquire at discount to replacement cost and reposit as rental (rather than condo) in a market with strong multifamily fundamentals.

stories.title: LogosFaith Development Expands into San Diego Market
stories.excerpt: LogosFaith Development, in partnership with San Diego’s Logan Temple AME Zion Church, commemorated the official groundbreaking on Logos Logan Legacy Place at the project site. The 43-home affordable housing community is located at 3186 and 3190 Franklin Ave. in San Diego’s Logan Heights neighborhood. The project marks the affordable housing developer’s expansion into the San Diego market. “Partnering with Logan AME Zion Church to bring this affordable housing project to San Diego is a meaningful milestone,” said Pastor Martin Porter, founder and CEO of LogosFaith Development. “Reflecting on Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s mountaintop speech and his vision of a better future, we too envisioned what was possible nearly six years ago. My goal was to build a development that would one day herald a new dawn for the city and our community – creating housing on faith-based land and helping address the housing crisis.” The project is built on church land and centers on the adaptive reuse of the church’s existing fellowship hall, preserving a longstanding neighborhood presence while creating new homes for local residents. Delivery is set for 2028. Pictured: Pastor Martin Porter (center in gray suit) with Rev. Dr. Virgil M. Ward (right in blue suit) joined by public officials and members of development team for groundbreaking of Logos Logan Legacy Place in San Diego’s Lincoln Heights neighborhood. The post LogosFaith Development Expands into San Diego Market appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LogosFaith Development breaking ground on 43-unit affordable housing in San Diego's Logan Heights.
Partnership with Logan Temple AME Zion Church; adaptive reuse of fellowship hall; delivery 2028.
Marks LogosFaith's first San Diego market entry; faith-based land development model.
stories.summary: LogosFaith Development, in partnership with Logan Temple AME Zion Church, is developing Logos Logan Legacy Place, a 43-unit affordable housing community in San Diego's Logan Heights neighborhood (3186–3190 Franklin Ave.). The project centers on adaptive reuse of the church's fellowship hall, preserving the congregation's neighborhood footprint while creating new housing. Delivery is slated for 2028; this marks LogosFaith's entry into San Diego.
stories.impact: Limited immediate relevance to market-rate multifamily development. However, the faith-based land partnership model and affordable-only positioning in an underserved neighborhood (Logan Heights) demonstrate creative entitlement pathways and reduced land cost that may signal where nonprofits and community partners capture development opportunities that market-rate developers face zoning/community resistance to; this can shift affordable supply dynamics in San Diego but does not directly affect market-rate rental demand or cap rates.

stories.title: PCCP Provides $164M Senior Loan for Paramus Multifamily Project
stories.excerpt: PCCP has provided a $163.9-million senior loan to a joint venture between Russo Development and Kushner Real Estate Group for the construction of The Paramus Chapter, a two-building, 426-unit multifamily project located at 2200 Bergen Town Center Dr. in Paramus, NJ. The project broke ground in July 2026, with completion anticipated for the fourth quarter of 2028. The Paramus Chapter will consist of two four-story buildings over concrete podiums, with approximately 5,300 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Building A will include 166 units, including 18 affordable units. Building B will include 260 units, with 38 affordable units. “We believe this financing represents an attractive opportunity to support an experienced joint venture in the development of a high-quality, Class A multifamily asset in one of Northern New Jersey’s strongest and most supply-constrained markets,” said Lia Barsanti, SVP with PCCP. “The Paramus Chapter is poised to benefit from its exceptional location and proximity to both regional employment centers and New York City.” The post PCCP Provides $164M Senior Loan for Paramus Multifamily Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PCCP provided $163.9M senior loan for The Paramus Chapter, 426-unit two-building project in Paramus, NJ.
Joint venture: Russo Development & Kushner Real Estate Group; 56 affordable units; ground-floor retail.
Broke ground July 2026; completion Q4 2028; lender cites supply-constrained Northern New Jersey market.
stories.summary: PCCP closed a $163.9M senior construction loan for The Paramus Chapter, a 426-unit, two-building multifamily project in Paramus, NJ (2200 Bergen Town Center Dr.), developed by a Russo Development and Kushner Real Estate Group joint venture. The project includes 56 affordable units across two four-story buildings over retail podiums and broke ground in July 2026, with completion targeted for Q4 2028. The lender emphasized strong market fundamentals and supply constraints in Northern New Jersey.
stories.impact: Northern New Jersey (Bergen County/Paramus area) is characterized as supply-constrained with strong fundamentals, attracting major construction financing from quality lenders at scale ($164M). This signals stable multifamily demand in the I-95 corridor near NYC and robust construction lending availability for experienced teams, supporting continued development starts in the submarket; lenders' confidence in completion and operational performance in a 'strong market' reflects tight supply thesis and pricing power expectations post-delivery in 2028.

stories.title: Blood Cancer Nonprofit DKMS Takes 15K SF at 115 Broadway
stories.excerpt: DKMS, an international nonprofit fighting blood cancer and blood disorders, has signed a new office lease within Manhattan’s Financial District. The organization took 15,000 square feet across the 14th floor of 115 Broadway. The 22-story building makes up half of the Gothic-style Trinity Centre owned by Capital Properties and Madison International Realty. It is unclear whether the deal will relocate or expand DKMS from its currently listed offices at 40 Fulton Street, several blocks east in the Financial District’s Seaport area. A spokesperson for DKMS did not immediately respond to a request for comment. CBRE’s Laurence Briody represented DKMS in the transaction, while a Colliers team of Aidan Campbell, Michael Joseph and JP Howard negotiated on the behalf of the landlords. Meanwhile, at Trinity Centre’s neighboring 111 Broadway, MaryAnne Gilmartin’s MAG Partners secured a seventh-floor lease spanning 4,066 square feet. The September deal marked a relocation for Gilmartin’s firm from Global Holdings’ 1250 Broadway, according to a spokesperson. MAG Partners was represented by the Kaufman Organization’s Michael Kaufman. Lease terms and asking rents for either office deal were not disclosed, but Class B office rents in the Financial District averaged $51.91 per square foot in the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers. The two fall arrivals at Trinity Centre are part of more than 100,000 square feet of leasing activity across 16 transactions recorded at the complex so far this year, according to a Colliers spokesperson. Work on the complex’s tenant amenity center was completed in August, and a collection of prebuilt office suites are on their way. Other fresh faces include advertiser LG Ad Solutions and Cook Law Firm at 115 Broadway, as well as consultancy company Perficient at 111 Broadway. Spokespeople for CBRE and the Kaufman Organization did not respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: DKMS blood cancer nonprofit leased 15,000 SF at 115 Broadway, Financial District Manhattan.
Lease on 14th floor of 22-story Trinity Centre; unclear if relocation or expansion from 40 Fulton St.
Building owned by Capital Properties and Madison International Realty; CBRE and Colliers represented parties.
stories.summary: DKMS, an international nonprofit fighting blood cancer and blood disorders, signed a 15,000 SF office lease on the 14th floor of 115 Broadway in Manhattan's Financial District. The 22-story Gothic-style building, part of Trinity Centre, is owned by Capital Properties and Madison International Realty. It is unclear whether DKMS is relocating from or expanding its current offices at 40 Fulton Street (also in Financial District/Seaport area).
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Nonprofit office leasing in Financial District does not signal residential demand or supply shifts; however, if DKMS is expanding (rather than relocating), it signals local job growth in the healthcare/nonprofit sector that could incrementally support residential demand in Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn subways-accessible neighborhoods. Insufficient evidence here to assess magnitude.

stories.title: Alexandria Reports Improved Sales and Leasing Amid Financial Hardships
stories.excerpt: Leasing has picked up steam for Alexandria Real Estate Equities, but the real estate investment trust continues to struggle with financial hemorrhaging. The REIT, which invests heavily in laboratories and life sciences facilities, reported a net loss of $638.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year when it lost $234.9 million, according to executives who spoke during Alexandria’s Tuesday earnings call. Funds from operations (FFO) landed at $264.4 million in the last quarter in contrast to the $296 million in the second quarter and $377.8 million year-over-year. Third-quarter revenue closed at $671 million compared to $662.7 million at the end of the second quarter but declined from $751.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. “Despite the current challenges in the life science real estate market, we continue to benefit from a high-quality tenant base with 57 percent of our annual rental revenue coming from the investment-grade or publicly traded large-cap tenants,” Joel Marcus, Alexandria’s executive chairman and founder, said during the call. Some items in its portfolio are in contract to sell, such as 421 Park Drive of the Alexandria Center for Life Science – Fenway Megacampus in Boston for about $136 million. The potential buyer for that deal was not disclosed. Alexandria sold $234 million in assets in the third quarter. Alexandria recorded 87.1 percent occupancy across its operating properties as leasing numbers have picked up, in the third quarter in particular. The REIT leased 1.2 million square feet of space in the three months ending Sept. 30, which exceeded 979,822 square feet signed on average in the six preceding quarters. The company will still face significant challenges in 2027, when up to 1.4 million square feet of leases will expire, and with it an estimated $100.5 million of annual rental revenue. bullets: Alexandria Real Estate (life sciences REIT) reported Q3 2026 net loss of $638.5M vs. $234.9M YoY.
FFO declined to $264.4M (Q3) from $377.8M (Q3 2025); revenue down to $671M from $751.9M.
Leasing improved; 57% of revenue from investment-grade/large-cap tenants; CEO acknowledges ongoing market challenges.
stories.summary: Alexandria Real Estate Equities reported a steep Q3 2026 net loss of $638.5M (vs. $234.9M loss in Q3 2025) and declining FFO ($264.4M vs. $377.8M YoY), despite sequential revenue growth to $671M. The life sciences REIT, which heavily invests in lab and research facilities, is benefiting from improved leasing activity and a high-quality, investment-grade tenant base (57% of annual rental revenue), but continues to face headwinds in the overall life sciences real estate market.
stories.impact: Alexandria's deepening losses and FFO compression reflect ongoing distress in life sciences real estate valuations and occupancy recovery, despite operational leasing improvements. This signals that even strong-tenant-base lab REITs face mark-to-market pressures and capitalization concerns; for multifamily developers, this underscores that capital markets remain bifurcated—life sciences/lab space is under stress while multifamily remains better-positioned. However, if lab/biotech tenants face financial pressure, it reduces downstream demand for life-science-adjacent residential in innovation hubs (Boston, San Diego, SF Bay), potentially softening multifamily fundamentals in those micro-markets.

stories.title: NBA Store Seeks New, Larger Location Up to 25K Square Feet
stories.excerpt: Jump ball. The NBA Store, which is operated by Fanatics-owned sports apparel company Lids, is planning to relocate from its longtime retail location at 545 Fifth Avenue into a larger space, Commercial Observer can first report. The retailer of team jerseys, collectibles and other basketball-related merchandise is exploring seven potential locations around Midtown Manhattan to expand from its current 15,000 square feet of sellable retail space that it has leased since 2015 at the corner of 45th Street and Fifth Avenue, a source familiar with the move told CO. Lids, which is leading the leasing process, is targeting 20,000 to 25,000 square feet of sellable space for the new store and is eyeing properties around Midtown, including in Times Square, along with several vacant buildings on Fifth Avenue, according to the source. The NBA Store lease is up at the Moinian Group-owned 545 Fifth Avenue in 2031, but the retailer is looking to have a new site lined up in about a year to have sufficient time to organize the build-out, the source said. Lids is looking to expand with a bigger “and more inviting ground floor” in the midst of a record year for the NBA Store, where business was bolstered this year by the New York Knicks capturing their first NBA title since 1973. In addition to adding space to sell jerseys and merchandise, the store’s operators hope to design an enhanced entrance. The NBA Store first launched in 1998 at 666 Fifth Avenue before setting up a smaller temporary store at 590 Fifth Avenue from 2011 to 2015, prior to relocating to 545 Fifth. The Moinian Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Fanatics declined to comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NBA Store (Lids/Fanatics) seeks relocation from 545 Fifth Ave. to 20,000–25,000 SF space in Midtown.
Current lease expires 2031; retailer targeting 7 locations in Midtown/Times Square/Fifth Avenue; 1-year timeline.
Expanding from 15,000 SF current footprint (leased since 2015); seeks larger branded retail presence.
stories.summary: The NBA Store, operated by Fanatics-owned Lids, is planning to relocate from its longtime 15,000 SF retail space at 545 Fifth Avenue (leased since 2015) to a larger venue. The retailer is exploring seven potential Midtown locations, including Times Square and vacant Fifth Avenue properties, targeting 20,000–25,000 SF of sellable space. Although the 545 Fifth Avenue lease does not expire until 2031, Lids is working toward a new location within one year to allow time for buildout.
stories.impact: Retail tenant expansion and relocation signals landlord/space availability in Midtown Manhattan and suggests retail market stabilization in prime corridors (Fifth Ave., Times Square). Early buildout timeline (12 months) reflects lender/landlord confidence in post-renovation performance. Limited direct multifamily impact, but retail health and real estate activity in Midtown support Office/entertainment district foot traffic and worker presence, indirectly supporting nearby residential demand in Murray Hill, Gramercy, and other East Midtown sublets.

stories.title: Shorenstein Buys Fully Leased SoHo Office Property From Tishman Speyer
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer has sold the 12-story, 155,000-square-foot office building at 148 Lafayette Street in SoHo, at the corner of Lafayette and Howard streets, to Shorenstein Properties for $132.5 million, or $866 per square foot, according to Tishman. The deal was repped by Newmark‘s Adam Spies, Doug Harmon, Adam Doneger, Marcella Fasulo, Avery Silverstein and Joshua King. Shorenstein outbid several institutional bidders, including private equity funds, for the building, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. The Real Deal was first to report the sale. Tishman is selling the property on a quick turnaround at a sizable profit, having purchased the building from Epic in May 2025 for $105.5 million, with $68.3 million of that coming in the form of an acquisition loan from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies. Prior to the 2025 purchase, Tishman had not bought an office building anywhere in the U.S. since 2021, and had not purchased an office building in Manhattan since 2019, according to previous reporting in Commercial Observer. The $105.5 million purchase price in 2025 represented a decline from the $126.5 million Epic paid for the building in 2012. “We acquired 148 Lafayette with a clear plan and executed it ahead of schedule, generating an attractive return for our investors,” Chris Shehadeh, senior managing director at Tishman, said in a statement. “This successful outcome reaffirms our conviction in the continued demand for premier office assets in prime Manhattan neighborhoods to both companies seeking exceptional work environments and institutional investors targeting high-quality real estate.” The building contains 141,359 square feet of office space, which is 100 percent leased to tenants including investment firm General Catalyst, artificial intelligence code review firm Graphite, coworking firm WeWork, cosmetics company Charlotte Tilbury, digital picture frame company Aura Frames and consulting firm Keystone. bullets: Shorenstein Properties purchased 148 Lafayette St., SoHo from Tishman Speyer for $132.5M ($866/SF).
Fully leased 12-story, 155,000 SF Class A office; Tishman purchased May 2025 for $105.5M.
Shorenstein outbid multiple institutional and PE bidders; Blackstone provided $68.3M acquisition debt to Tishman.
stories.summary: Shorenstein Properties acquired 148 Lafayette Street in SoHo from Tishman Speyer for $132.5M ($866 per SF), a fully leased 12-story, 155,000 SF Class A office building at the corner of Lafayette and Howard streets. Tishman purchased the property from Epic in May 2025 for $105.5M, financed partly by a $68.3M Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies acquisition loan. Shorenstein outbid several private equity and institutional bidders.
stories.impact: Institutional capital (Shorenstein) is actively acquiring fully-leased, trophy Manhattan office assets at scale, signaling renewed conviction in A-tier office fundamentals and the existence of cash-rich buyers with return expectations tied to long-term tenant stability rather than value-add repositioning. This transaction (nearly identical to Article 1) reinforces that capital will flow to super-prime, transit-proximate, tenant-occupied office in gateway metros, but underscores that this is narrow-band recovery—not a broad office market turnaround. Multifamily developers should note that institutional capital deployed in trophy office is capital not deployed in multifamily acquisitions; watch for shifts in buyer appetite if office fundamentals roll over further.

stories.title: Welltower Earnings Boosted by Senior Housing Acquisitions
stories.excerpt: Welltower, the country’s largest senior housing landlord, reported another strong quarter with increased pricing power and ample acquisitions. During its third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday morning, the Ohio-based real estate investment trust (REIT) reported its profits were up 24.6 percent per share year-over-year, with occupancy throughout its portfolio at 88 percent. Welltower continues to buy properties at a healthy clip, while it executes a long-term move to offload a significant slice of its outpatient medical properties. Welltower’s normalized funds from operations (FFO) were $1.67 per share, up 24.6 percent annually. This company figure excludes line items like debt payments, transactions costs and legal fees. The REIT’s revenue totaled $3.7 billion between July and September, up roughly 38 percent from $2.7 billion over the same three-month period in 2025. Instead of large-scale mergers and acquisitions — which Shankh Mitra, CEO of Welltower, said they “avoid like the plague” — the REIT has completed 196 different transactions this year, with $21 billion in investments completed or under contract so far. Within the third quarter, Welltower acquired 43 senior housing properties for $2.7 billion. Despite this activity, Mitra told investors that it acquires less than 3 percent of the assets it screens. Welltower is primed to buy on distress, said Nikhil Chaudhri, co-president and chief investment officer of Welltower, noting the roughly $8 billion of U.S. senior housing debt due in 2026. “While some owners may recapitalize, most will sell as the impact of rising rates offsets improved industry fundamentals,” Chaudhri said. “That is where Welltower comes in.” Welltower has offloaded $2.1 billion worth of outpatient medical assets so far this year, including 25 properties within the quarter. bullets: Welltower reported Q3 2026 FFO up 24.6% YoY to $1.67/share; revenue $3.7B, up 38% YoY.
88% occupancy across portfolio; completed 196 transactions totaling $21B in acquisitions; strong pricing power.
Executing strategic exit from outpatient medical properties; CEO avoids large M&A; focused on bolt-on acquisitions.
stories.summary: Welltower, the nation's largest senior housing landlord, reported robust Q3 2026 results with normalized FFO of $1.67 per share (up 24.6% YoY) and revenue of $3.7B (up 38% YoY). The Ohio-based REIT maintains 88% portfolio occupancy and has completed 196 transactions totaling $21B in investments this year. CEO Shankh Mitra stated the company avoids large-scale M&A, instead pursuing disciplined bolt-on acquisitions while divesting outpatient medical properties.
stories.impact: Welltower's strong FFO growth, high occupancy, and aggressive acquisition pace ($21B in 196 deals) signal robust senior housing fundamentals and lender/operator confidence in aging demographics and pricing power. For multifamily developers, this underscores that senior housing (55+, assisted living, memory care) is attracting institutional capital and delivering strong returns; consider whether mixed-age, mixed-income multifamily assets are being overshadowed by demographic tailwinds favoring age-restricted housing. Additionally, Welltower's disciplined, bolt-on acquisition strategy and exit from outpatient medical suggests selective capital deployment—strong performers are capital-light, not capital-heavy on new development.
